Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.

Also: golden tests are MANDATORY for `flutter_app/lib/` UI work — this PR touches `packages/fa_ui`, not `flutter_app/lib/`. The changed picker tiles now render disabled tiles — does fa_ui have golden tests? Let me check packages/fa_ui/test for golden tests.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Now some sharper checks:

**1. `_hasSsoFlow` on the tooltip:** `Tooltip` wraps the whole `ListTile`. A disabled ListTile ignores pointer events? No — `enabled: false` ListTile still absorbs taps (onTap null). Tooltip still shows on hover since the tile itself is hoverable. In the tests `find.byTooltip` finds it. On mobile, long-press shows tooltip. OK.

**2. Subtle UX inconsistency:** host-callback path pops the picker BEFORE running the callback (`Navigator.of(context).pop(); onAiinConnect!();`), while default-flow path keeps the picker mounted. Different host integration semantics, but that's deliberate (default flows push their own pages). OK.

**3. `Tooltip` around disabled tile — the trailing chevron stays colored** — cosmetic.

**4. THE `onDeviceRoutes` and editor path unchanged.** OK.

**5. `visiblePresets` ordering with disabled tiles** — the four SSO tiles stay interleaved in default order. In the ChatGPT test, "the four extra disabled tiles push DIAL below the lazy-build window" — noted in test comment. Fine.

**6. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.
