## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

Important: "`lib/` is pure Dart: no `dart:io`". The PR adds fa_ui package code — the conditional export handles web. `packages/fa_ui` is a Flutter package, not `lib/` of the root. The conditional export (`sso_desktop_flows_stub.dart if (dart.library.io)`) is the standard pattern. Good.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

- **CodeMie** — the CLI's `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` (browser SSO, localhost callback) → org lands as a custom entry (`<org>/code-assistant-api/v1`), session cookie in the canonical `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot (`registry.rememberKey`), model picked from `fetchCodeMieModels` (manual-entry fallback when the list fetch fails). A re-sign-in on a known endpoint refreshes that entry's key in place (CLI re-auth semantics: name/model kept, no model re-pick).
- **ChatGPT (Codex)** — the CLI's `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (PKCE + loopback) → `chatgpt-codex` entry named after the account email, encoded credential blob remembered + persisted entry-scoped (`CustomProviderRegistry.keyNameFor(chatGptCodexBaseUrl, providerName: name)` — byte-identical with the CLI/app slot), default model `chatGptCodexDefaultModel`.
- **AIIN** — the CLI's `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (sign-in + key auto-register) → entry named after the account email, `sk-aiin-…` key entry-scoped, model picked from `/v1/models`.
- **Copilot** — the existing `showCopilotConnectSheet` with the default fa_llm device-flow wiring (github.com CORS keeps web out, snack says so) → `copilot-<login>` entry (`kind: copilot` dispatch hint), GitHub token entry-scoped (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`, Keychain-first/saved-keys-fallback) via the public `FaUiSso.landCopilotConnect`.

Every flow lands through the **existing store abstractions** — `ProviderRegistry`, `KeychainStore`, `SessionKeysStore` — and reports through `onConnected`; the host reconfigures its own agent loop from the registry (fa_ui stays host-agnostic).

**Option C (done regardless):** a sign-in tile without any flow now renders **disabled under a tooltip** ("Sign-in flow not available in this app", `ssoFlowUnavailableTooltip` en/ru) instead of being silently hidden; catalog/`FA_PROVIDERS`-filtered tiles still hide (build-intentional scoping) but now emit a debug log naming every filtered tile.

## Architecture-boundary contract (owner note 16:09:49Z) — compliance

- **Logic reused from core/CLI, zero re-implementation**: fa_ui calls the CLI's exported flow functions (`runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow`, `runAiinConnectCliFlow` from `lib/io.dart`) and the core token/key-slot machinery (`CustomProviderRegistry.keyNameFor`/`copilotEntryKeyName`, `fetchCodeMieModels`, `fetchModelsForEndpoint`, `chatGptCodexDefaultModel`). Endpoints, token exchange, key-slot naming, error surfaces stay in core; fa_ui adds presentation + platform bridges (the conditional `sso_desktop_flows_io.dart`/`_stub.dart` pair, web reports the platform as unsupported).
- **Interpretation note**: the only new parsing in fa_ui is the JWT-`email` claim reader seeding ChatGPT/AIIN entry names (display identity, not a security path); the flutter_app keeps a private copy of the same helper today.
- **Interpretation note**: fa_ui defaults reuse-on-match for re-auth — CodeMie by endpoint, ChatGPT/AIIN/Copilot by (name + endpoint), matching the CLI/app re-auth semantics. The flutter_app keeps its richer flows (iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, WebView fallbacks, extension cookie branch, `AgentService` reconfigure) — its explicit callbacks override the bundle per provider, unchanged.

## Honest scope notes (AC1 vs platforms)

- AC1 ("all four tiles complete sign-in end-to-end on macOS, keys in the canonical slot") is delivered **on desktop** (macOS/Windows/Linux — the CLI's browser + loopback flows, the same ones the CLI runs today). On iOS/Android the desktop hop would print the URL instead of launching the browser (the CLI `openBrowser` shells out) — mobile hosts keep their WebView/auth-session callbacks; wiring those surfaces as fa_ui platform bridges is the natural follow-up.
- AC3 delivered in both offered forms (tooltip + log line).
- Not covered: per-account-suffixed CodeMie slots (the bundle writes the canonical `FA_KEY_<HOST>`; the CLI's named-account variants are a host override for now), and richer CodeMie name/project pickers (the bundle names the entry by org host).

- `flutter test test/sso_flows_test.dart test/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **20/20 green** (10 new flow tests: landing, re-auth, cancel, unsupported-platform snack, keychain-first slot via mocked `fah/keychain`; picker option-C tile states, sso-bundle enablement, filter-hide + log).
- Full `packages/fa_ui` suite: **508 passed / 47 failed — the 47 are pre-existing** `fa_chat_drop_test.dart` platform-channel failures, verified byte-identical (same 47) on pristine `origin/main` with this diff stashed.
- `dart analyze` over `packages/fa_ui/lib` + the touched tests: zero findings in changed files (the 4 remaining findings are pre-existing in `chat_surface_handlers.dart`/`trajectory_view.dart`, untouched).
- No live macOS end-to-end sign-in was run from this lane (needs real enterprise credentials + GUI); the PR's own CI is the integration gate.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Also there's 1 comment on the issue — the "owner note 16:09:49Z" (architecture-boundary contract). Let me fetch issue comments to confirm the boundary contract.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

The PR honestly discloses AC1 is delivered on desktop only (mobile would print the URL). This matches "on macOS" (desktop) — macOS IS desktop, so AC1 as literally written ("end-to-end on macOS") is arguably delivered. The PR's disclosure is conservative. OK.

Also there's 1 comment on the issue — the "owner note 16:09:49Z" (architecture-boundary contract). Let me fetch issue comments to confirm the boundary contract.

Summary

Embedding `fa_ui` in a thin-client host app (YoClip Studio, `packages/yoclip_player`) — the **Add provider** catalog silently hides **every SSO-backed tile**: AIIN, ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot, and CodeMie. Only API-key tiles (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom) are shown, plus OpenRouter OAuth because the host implements its own OAuth capture.

The reason: each SSO tile is gated on a **host callback** (`onCodeMieSso`, `onCopilotConnect`, the ChatGPT OAuth callback, the AIIN callback). When the host passes `null`, the tile is hidden. That is reasonable gating — but it pushes the full enterprise sign-in flows (device flow, OAuth handshake, key storage, re-auth) onto **every host that embeds fa_ui**. Those flows are exactly the logic a thin client should NOT re-implement: they are security-sensitive, provider-specific, and already implemented once in the CLI/harness.

**Ask:** extract the SSO sign-in flows into `fa_ui` (or a small companion package) as ready-made, host-configurable implementations, so enabling CodeMie/Copilot/ChatGPT/AIIN in a new host is a few lines — not a re-implementation.

## Environment

- Harness pin: `b904430cadc15d53abc1e0d3cc736eacb8a44ed0` (v1.0.517 release commit) — `flutter_agent_harness`, `fa_ui`, `fa_llm` from one git checkout
- Host: `yoclip_player` (Flutter desktop, macOS arm64, debug via `flutter run`), embeds `ProvidersSection` / `AddProviderPicker` through `FaUiThemeProvider` + host callbacks
- Agent loop on the host side: `adk_dart 2026.7.11` (separate concern, see "Related gaps")

## Reproduction

1. Open the host app → Settings → Providers → **Add provider**
2. The catalog lists only: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DIAL, Kimi Code, MiniMax, Z.AI, Ollama Cloud, Custom
3. AIIN / ChatGPT (Codex) / GitHub Copilot / CodeMie are absent — no error, no log line explains the filtering

Observed on v1.0.517; the host implements only API-key flows plus a custom OpenRouter OAuth capture.

## Root cause (code walk at `b904430ca`)

`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/add_provider_picker.dart`:

- `defaultAddProviderPresets` (lines ~60–126) **does contain** the SSO presets, e.g.
  ```dart
  AddProviderPreset(
    key: 'codemie',
    name: 'CodeMie',
    description: 'Enterprise SSO sign-in',
    icon: Icons.security_outlined,
  ),
  ```
- The visibility rule (line 176):
  ```dart
  return spec.visible && harness.providerEnabledInBuild(spec.name);
  ```
- Callback contracts (lines ~212–263): *"Tapping CodeMie calls `onCodeMieSso` — the host should launch the SSO flow"*; *"When null, the ChatGPT tile is hidden"*; *"When null, the Copilot tile is hidden"*; AIIN likewise.

So a host that has not implemented the flows gets the tiles silently removed. Users see a picker that looks like the providers don't exist — and host developers get no hint either (nothing is logged when a tile is filtered).

## Why this matters

- Our architecture (and presumably others'): the embedding client stays **minimal — rendering and wiring only**. Enterprise SSO / device flows / OAuth + keychain storage are harness-domain logic.
- Re-implementing them per host invites exactly the bug class seen in #1194 (AIIN add-provider: *"sign-in completes but the provider is never added"*).
- The CLI already has all these flows working (see key slots `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AIIN_API_KEY`, canonical CodeMie slots in the macOS Keychain). The SDK/ui layer just doesn't expose them.

## Proposal (in order of preference)

**A. Flows live in fa_ui.** Ship default implementations a host enables with a one-liner, e.g. `FaUiSso.installed(presets: [...])` — CodeMie enterprise SSO, Copilot device flow, ChatGPT OAuth, AIIN auto-register — reusing the CLI's flow logic, storing keys through the host's `Session…

Now I have the actual issue ACs:

- **AC1**: A host with no custom flow code sees all four SSO tiles and each completes sign-in end-to-end on macOS, storing keys in the canonical slot.
- **AC2**: A fresh host can enable SSO providers with ≤ a few lines.
- **AC3**: Filtered tiles are explainable (log line and/or disabled-with-tooltip).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Copilot landing logic is now forked between fa_ui and flutter_app — the #1194 drift class**

`landCopilotConnect` re-implements the landing block of the app's `runCopilotConnectFlow` (`flutter_app/lib/services/copilot_connect_flow.dart`): the (name + endpoint) re-auth match, the `kind: copilotDispatchHint` add, `rememberKey`, and the Keychain-first/saved-keys-fallback entry-scoped persist. Today they are byte-equivalent — but they are two independent copies of security-adjacent store-write logic. If one side changes (slot naming, fallback order, requiresKey marker), the other silently diverges — exactly the "divergent implementations, one silently stale" bug class the owner's architecture-boundary note on #1321 warns about.

Same pattern, smaller blast radius: `_chatGptEmail` and `_uniqueEntryName` duplicate the private helpers in `flutter_app/lib/services/chatgpt_oauth_flow.dart`, and `_persistEntryScopedKey` duplicates `_persistEntryKey` / the AIIN flow's inline persist.

Since `landCopilotConnect` is already public and behavior-identical, the app can delegate with no functional change:

```dart
// flutter_app/lib/services/copilot_connect_flow.dart
final provider =
    await FaUiSso.landCopilotConnect(
      registry,
      connect,
      keychain: keychain,
      sessionKeys: sessionKeys,
    );
if (provider == null) return false;
// … service reconfigure + lastConnection stay app-side
```

(The PR deliberately leaves the app untouched and discloses the divergence — fair — but then the follow-up should be tracked, or better, done in this PR while the two copies are provably identical.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: use the exported `chatgptCodexDispatchHint` instead of the string literal**

The `kind` value is the model-list dispatch's identity hint: `_CodexDialect.matches(baseUrl, provider)` compares against `chatgptCodexDispatchHint` (`lib/src/providers/models_for_endpoint.dart`, exported via `flutter_agent_harness.dart`, which this file already imports). Hardcoding `'chatgpt-codex'` works today but re-couples the flow to the literal — if the hint constant ever changes, the entry silently drops off the Codex wire with no compile-time signal. The flutter_app flow uses the constant (`kind: chatgptCodexDispatchHint`), so this also keeps the two writers identical:

```dart
kind: chatgptCodexDispatchHint,
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: two registries, one page — nothing ties `sso.registry` to the picker's `registry`**

`FaUiSso` carries its own required `registry`, and the page has its own nullable `registry` (used by the key-based presets' editor and `landProviderResult`). The blessed one-liner passes the same store to both, but nothing enforces it: a host can construct `AddProviderPresetPickerPage(registry: a, sso: FaUiSso(registry: b))` and SSO landings go to `b` while key-based saves go to `a` — the provider list (driven by one of them) silently misses entries. With `registry: null` + `sso:` given, key-based presets even edit a throwaway `ProviderRegistry.inMemory()` while SSO entries persist into `sso.registry`.

Options, cheapest first:
- document on the `sso` field that it must be built around the same `ProviderRegistry` instance the page receives; or
- debug-mode assert in the constructor/build (`assert(sso == null || registry == null || identical(...))` — note `FaUiSso` doesn't expose its registry; adding a getter would enable this); or
- long-term, let the page derive the bundle: `AddProviderPresetPickerPage.ssoFromRegistry`.

Fine to defer, but worth a doc line now so the contract is at least written down where hosts will read it.

**A. `connectCodeMie` — `_hostOf(orgUrl)` name vs `credentials.apiUrl`-derived baseUrl.** If the caller passes a custom orgUrl (say `https://codemie.other.com`), the CLI flow builds apiUrl from it → baseUrl = `<apiUrl>/v1` → name = host of orgUrl. Consistent. But `connectCodeMie(context)` — the picker path always uses the default orgUrl; orgUrl param is for hosts. OK.

**B. `connectCodeMie` re-auth: NO entry-scoped/host keychain persistence when registry has no keychain.** `registry.rememberKey(existing.id, credentials.authToken)` — session-only if registry in-memory or no keychain. For CodeMie the CLI writes the canonical `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot in the secure store. The registry's rememberKey does that only when `_useKeychain` (set during load when keychain injected+available). For a thin-client host that loads the registry WITH keychain — fine. OK — matches "registry.rememberKey" contract as described. Fine.

**C. Missing `context.mounted` guard in `_runDesktopFlow` after the long browser wait — snack shown only if mounted; else silently returns null.** Handled.

**D. `_fetchLenient` catches `on Object` — swallows everything including programming errors.** It's the documented convention (CLI/app). OK.

**E. `_chatGptEmail` — `jsonDecode` may return non-Map → `payload['email']` throws TypeError, caught by `on Object` → null. OK.

**F. `_uniqueEntryName` infinite loop?** `while (clash != null && clash.baseUrl != baseUrl) { name = '$identity-${suffix++}'; ... }` — suffix increments; byName('identity-2'), ('identity-3')... terminates when a name is free or matches same endpoint. Terminates. But note `suffix++` post-increment inside interpolation: `'$identity-${suffix++}'` — first iteration name becomes `identity-2` (suffix was 2 → uses 2 then becomes 3). OK.

**G. `_landEntry` in ChatGPT flow — `kind` on the update path:** `kind: existing.kind ?? kind`. Hmm wait — for ChatGPT update-in-place (re-auth), if existing.kind is null (entry created by older version or manually), this sets kind='chatgpt-codex'. It also would OVERRIDE... no, `??` keeps existing.kind when non-null. But hold on — what if an existing entry named `dev@acme.com` on chatgpt endpoint has kind 'copilot'? Absurd edge. Skip.

**H. In `connectChatGpt`, missing mounted check between `_runDesktopFlow` (which can take minutes) and `_landEntry`:** `_landEntry` doesn't use context. `showFahSnack` guarded. OK.

**I. `connectChatGpt` — the snack says 'ChatGPT connected' — fine.

**J. POTENTIAL ISSUE — `connectChatGpt` does not check `credentials.accessToken` emptiness.** `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` returns null on failure; credentials non-null → has tokens. OK.

**K. POTENTIAL ISSUE — `_persistEntryScopedKey` writes the FULL credential blob (containing refresh token) to the sessionKeys store** — the saved-keys store UI displays saved keys? "Values must never reach the UI" for KeychainStore. SessionKeysStore — the Keys settings section lists key NAMES, not values presumably. Consistent with app behavior (`_persistEntryKey` writes encoded blob to sessionKeys too). OK — same as app.

**L. Copilot flow `connectCopilot` — `copilotCallbacks` null → builds default. The PR's `CopilotConnectCallbacks` requires `fetchModels` etc. — all provided. `showCopilotConnectSheet` — needs `context`; mounted? called synchronously after kIsWeb check — context is the picker's, mounted. During the sheet, user might navigate... fine.

**M. `landCopilotConnect` — static, uses `registry.providers.where(...)` — matches app. It does NOT notify/`onConnected` internally — `connectCopilot` calls `_notify(provider)` after. But `landCopilotConnect` is PUBLIC and documented "a host running the sheet with its own callbacks lands through the same helper" — a host calling it directly gets NO onConnected notification (it's an instance callback; the static can't call it). Documented behavior gap — minor; the host has the result in hand. Suggestion-level at most.

**N. Now — a REAL correctness question: `connectCodeMie` re-auth match by `byBaseUrl` (endpoint match), but `_landEntry` for fresh connect matches by name+endpoint. Consider: registry has an entry named 'X' on `https://other.com/v1` AND the user connects CodeMie org `codemie.lab.epam.com` → fresh path: name = `_uniqueEntryName(registry, 'codemie.lab.epam.com', baseUrl)` — 'codemie.lab.epam.com' not taken → fine.

Then the cookie stays session-only while ChatGPT/AIIN flows DO persist entry-scoped via `_persistEntryScopedKey`. Inconsistent persistence guarantees between flows given the same bundle wiring. Hmm — but the PR description says CodeMie uses "the canonical FA_KEY_<HOST> slot (registry.rememberKey)" — deliberate: canonical slot = registry-managed. And hosts are told registry should be loaded with keychain. It's a documented contract; the session-only degradation is the registry's documented behavior (issue #329 requires UI to state it plainly — the snack says 'CodeMie connected' either way). ## PR #1326 Review Summary — `[fa_ui] FaUiSso: ready-made CodeMie/ChatGPT/Copilot/AIIN sign-in flows`

**Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES`** (1 blocking, 2 important, 5 suggestions). CI: 10/10 checks green, no CI failures in input.

**What's good:** the PR honors the owner's architecture-boundary contract — flow logic is genuinely reused from core/CLI (`runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` etc.), key slots are byte-identical with CLI/app (`keyNameFor(baseUrl, providerName:)`, `copilotEntryKeyName`), stores are the existing abstractions, option-C tile states + `FA_PROVIDERS` logging match issue #1321's ACs, and 10 new flow tests cover landing/re-auth/cancel/web-gate/keychain-first. I verified the ChatGPT slot naming is truly byte-identical with the app's `chatgptEntryKeyName`, and that the flutter_app (all four explicit callbacks) is behaviorally unaffected.

**🚨 Blocking:** `sso_desktop_flows_io.dart` is selected by `if (dart.library.io)` — true on **iOS/Android too**, not just desktop. There `openBrowser` returns false, and fa_ui's `onStatus` is a `kDebugMode`-only `debugPrint`, so the CodeMie/ChatGPT/AIIN tiles (enabled whenever `sso != null`, any platform) run a silent 5-minute hang: no browser, no log, no snack, no entry. A mobile host following the advertised one-liner ships three dead sign-in tiles — worse than the pre-PR hidden state and against option C's "never silent" principle. Fix is small: gate the hops off mobile → the existing `UnsupportedError` snack path explains it.

**⚠️ Important:** (1) `_runDesktopFlow` catches only `UnsupportedError` — a loopback `SocketException` from `server.start()` escapes with no snack (the CLI wraps the same flows in a broad catch); (2) `landCopilotConnect`/`_chatGptEmail`/`_uniqueEntryName` are now forked between fa_ui and flutter_app — the app should delegate to the public helper before the copies drift (the exact #1194 divergent-implementation class the owner's boundary note warns about).

**💡 Suggestions:** use the exported `chatgptCodexDispatchHint` const instead of the `'chatgpt-codex'` literal; actually assert the AC3 debug log in the "and is logged" test; document/assert `sso.registry` vs the page's `registry` (two stores, one page); add in-flight feedback + re-entrancy guard during the up-to-5-minute desktop hop; fix the export-list alphabetical order.

(Note: `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` markers in my transcript are my tooling's output-layer redaction of `apiKey` expressions — the actual source correctly reads `result.apiKey.raw` and handles secrets properly; nothing is logged or leaked.)
